Crocodile Capture & Relocation

Capture is the last resort. We assess the animal, confirm approvals, then trap or noose, secure and relocate it, and report back.

Where we work

Across the north

Based in Howard Springs, just outside Darwin, we service projects throughout the Northern Territory, Western Australia and Queensland — including remote and fly-in sites.

  • Northern Territory — home base
  • Western Australia & Queensland
  • Outside regular service area

Why it matters

Know what you’re working beside

Crocodiles are ambush predators that live in rivers, billabongs, estuaries and coastal waters across the north.

~100,000

estimated saltwater crocodiles in the wild in the Northern Territory

6 m

maximum length a saltwater crocodile can reach

Night

is when crocodiles are often most active — and hardest to see

Sources: Northern Territory Government (nt.gov.au) crocodile facts; University of Florida IFAS, Counting and Capturing Crocodilians.

How we control the risk

The CSA control ladder

We work down the ladder, starting with the least invasive control that keeps people safe. Capture sits at the bottom — it’s the last resort, not the default.

See our services
  1. 1AvoidMost preferred

    Plan the work away from the water’s edge: exclusion zones, timing, camp and access siting.

  2. 2Watch

    Dedicated spotters and overwatch with stop-work authority when crews must be near water.

  3. 3Train

    Toolbox talks and awareness training so every worker recognises and responds to the risk.

  4. 4RemoveLast resort

    Capture and relocation — only when other controls are impractical, and fully permitted.

Our story

Practical. Experienced. On site.

Crocodile Safety Australia helps government and industry work safely where crocodiles, snakes and other wildlife live. We read the site, understand the animals and design controls that fit the way your crew actually works.

Founded by Chris Peberdy in Darwin in 2002, CSA delivers expert reptile and wildlife handling, risk management, training, husbandry and advisory services to government and non-government organisations across the NT, WA and QLD.

Chris is the operator you deal with — from a 4.5-metre saltwater crocodile flown to Sydney (now known as Elvis) to Kakadu’s crocodile SOPs and on-set safety for the BBC and National Geographic.

Credentials

  • Licensed & insured
  • WHS-compliant
  • SOPs, SWMS & risk assessments
